read_scope.notes: Read all 22 pages, including the abstract, main text, references, and Appendices A–G. Visually inspected individual rendered PDF pages 1–22, including Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12. Consulted the frozen paper.tex, specificity_results.tex, and specificity_estimator_details.tex to resolve wording, notation, and cross-references. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Extraction and rendering used the isolated /tmp/editorial_r32_b directory. Independently computed the supplied PDF SHA256; no other reviews or manuscript versions were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: The English is precise, fluent, and unusually economical for the number of distinctions maintained. Section 4.1 explains contrasts through a concrete lightness gap before introducing symbols; Section 5.4 explains why shrinking a near-unit aligned response can reduce total error. Qualifications are generally attached to the claims they constrain. The compressed ratio/cosine sentence in Section 5.2 is a localized exception because it leaves the reported estimator variant unclear.
score_reasons.structure: The manuscript progresses coherently from the motivating distinction through the experimental arms, feature interpretation, score intuition, inference, and results. Primary model comparisons precede explicitly retrospective pair, calibration, and source checks. Tables 4 and 5 make the changes in ordering and inferential conclusions easy to follow. Derivations and historical cohorts are appropriately separated into appendices; the main narrative does not depend on reading them. The discussion could make its synthesis one step more explicit without adding length.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: A graduate-level reader can recover the target, intervention, and main findings without repository access. The abstract identifies the design, shared fraction, pair weakness, calibration result, and perceptual limit. Table 1 interprets the feature families; Section 4.1 gives the 1/0/1 error example; Section 4.2 distinguishes the theoretical no-contrast benchmark from the observed generic arm. Figure captions explain centering, projection limits, and negative corrected errors. The small remaining accessibility gap is the ambiguous ordinary-versus-corrected cosine reference in Section 5.2.
score_reasons.engagement: The paper sustains a clear question: a name response may be substantial without reproducing labeled painter differences. Figure 1 provides inspectable examples, Figure 2 reveals the separation of Cézanne and compression of nearby painters, and Figure 3 makes the aggregate/pair discrepancy concrete. The FLUX versus GPT Image 2 calibration result and the source-correction comparison provide consequential turns without claiming better images or statistical superiority. The discussion is concise but could state more directly what each evaluation choice rewards.

strengths: The opening Monet–Sisley example makes the difference between collection proximity and labeled painter contrasts concrete before any notation appears.
Section 4.1 combines a measured lightness example with the no-distinction/exact/doubled-response error example, giving readers a useful interpretation of both beta and D.

The main figures and tables are legible and purposeful. Figure 2 supplies magnified M/S/P details, Figure 3 prints values in the heatmap cells, and Table 4 visibly separates scene averaging from calibration.

The narrative consistently distinguishes the lowest point estimate from resolved comparisons. Table 5 explicitly shows which intervals change after source correction and identifies the retrospective status of those checks.

Reference provenance, fixed-scene inference, two-repeat assumptions, feature-space calibration, and the absence of perceptual validation are described in the main text without requiring the technical appendices.

findings.location: Section 5.2, p. 8, specificity_results.tex lines 52–55; Appendix B, pp. 13–14, paper.tex lines 451–456
findings.issue: The sentence reporting squared-magnitude ratios of 1.96–4.14 and cosines of .689–.930 does not explicitly identify the ratio numerator or which cosine estimator produced the reported range. Appendix B discusses both an ordinary repeat-averaged cosine and a separate cross-repeat diagnostic.
findings.reader_effect: A reader can understand the qualitative common-response result, but cannot unambiguously connect these numerical ranges to the two estimator descriptions or tell whether the quoted cosine retains shared-baseline noise.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the compressed sentence with wording that explicitly says named-to-generic squared-magnitude ratio and identifies the reported cosine as ordinary repeat-averaged or cross-repeat corrected, as appropriate. Tie that named variant to the Appendix B formula. This can replace the existing sentence without adding a table or increasing the page count.

findings.location: Section 6, p. 10, first paragraph, paper.tex lines 310–315
findings.issue: The discussion ends its synthesis of averaging and calibration with the general statement that they reward different properties of the same images, without naming those properties at this final interpretive point.
findings.reader_effect: The reader must reconstruct the distinction from Section 5.4 precisely where the discussion could leave a compact, memorable interpretation of the changed ordering.
findings.suggested_change: Replace that general clause with a similarly short explicit distinction, such as: Scene averaging evaluates agreement of the mean painter pattern; calibration evaluates fit after adjusting contrast size. Retain the existing separation of these evaluation choices and the existing limits on claims about images.

summary: Excellent editorial presentation of a bounded feature-space comparison. The main study and its findings stand on their own, the figures reward inspection, and the primary-versus-retrospective distinction is clear. Only localized clarification of a diagnostic estimator and the discussion synthesis is needed; no new experiments, evidence, or manuscript expansion is warranted by this review.
